subject: Forecast check: commit drift & early churn flags
thread_content:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Julie Smith <j.smith@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Forecast check: commit drift & early churn flags

Hi Julie —

Quick check-in on the Q4 renewal/commit we have in the forecast (RDW-ACME-2027Q4). Finance flagged a small but material drift vs. the commit we modelled last quarter. Attached is a one-page commit summary and a usage snapshot that shows the last 6 weeks. Can you confirm the current expected ARR/seat count for the 12/31 renewal?

Specific asks:
- Confirm (by EOD Mon) the committed ARR number you expect to finalize for Q4.
- If there are procurement timing concerns, flag procurement contact so we can align billing cadence.
- If usage is expected to drop, any plan/mechanism to keep coverage (e.g., consolidation, seat reallocation) would help our forecast.

Ive looped in Ben for any credit/obligation questions and Naomi from Finance for reforecasting.

Attachments: ACME_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF), commit_summary_Q4.csv (CSV), usage_trend_snapshot.png (PNG)

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

---
From: Julie Smith <j.smith@acme-corp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Forecast check: commit drift & early churn flags

Thanks Tessa — quick reply while I pull numbers.

Short answers:
- We do expect a reduction in usage for one business unit (Digital Ads) starting mid-November; forecasted reduction ~12% vs prior quarter.
- Procurement is still finalizing PO timing; they indicate a hold until 11/22 while budget approvals come through.

Question for your team: what flexibility do we have on mid-quarter commit adjustments without impacting pricing tiers? Procurement also asked whether usage smoothing options exist so we don't get hit with seat churn reporting.

Julie
Head of Platform Operations
ACME Corp

---
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Forecast check: commit drift & early churn flags

Tessa / Ben —

I pulled the numbers against our current forecast. If ACME proceeds with the indicated 12% usage reduction for Digital Ads and the PO slips to 11/22, we see a potential -$86k ARR impact on the Q4 committed pipe (net of existing credits/overage). That moves the probability-weighted forecast down by ~6 points for the quarter.

Recommendations:
- Ask for a soft-commit confirmation by 11/18 to lock the forecast for finance close.
- Offer a smoothing option (annualized billing with quarter-level true-up) to alleviate procurement timing — this avoids an immediate downgrade in the forecast if procurement signs late.
- If ACME needs a temporary credit for November consumption, propose a capped concession (e.g., credit up to $12k) tied to execution of PO by 11/22. Finance can approve up to that amount with a reconciliation clause.

Im away for part of tomorrow afternoon but can sign off on the concession if Ben vets the commercial language.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Finance Ops
Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Julie Smith <j.smith@acme-corp.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Forecast check: commit drift & early churn flags

Julie — appreciate the visibility. We have two pragmatic options that should keep you on the current pricing tier while accommodating procurement timing:

1) Smoothing addendum: annualized commitment with quarterly true-up. No pricing change. If PO comes late, November consumption gets applied to the annualized amount and reconciled at quarter-end.

2) Short-term credit: one-time capped credit (up to $12k) if PO is fully executed by 11/22 and your team signs the smoothing addendum. Reconciliation clause applies; any excess consumption converted back to standard billing after Q4.

Next steps I suggest:
- Julie: confirm whether Procurement can accept a 30-minute call tomorrow to review the smoothing addendum language.
- Tessa: if Procurement needs a redline, Ill prepare a short addendum and Naomi will approve the finance-side terms.

Ill draft the addendum now and post the link here once ready: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyzACMEForecast

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
